title: !important and why to avoid routine use
learningObjectives: Explain how !important changes cascade priority and choose maintainable alternatives for ordinary styling conflicts.

understand.concept: Appending !important to a declaration marks it important in the cascade. It changes the priority order and can make ordinary overrides ineffective until the conflict is resolved at the appropriate priority level.
understand.whyItMatters: Frequent use creates hard-to-maintain stylesheets, makes component overrides difficult, and can interfere with user accessibility preferences.
understand.analogy: It is like marking an instruction as high priority. If every instruction is marked urgent, resolving conflicts becomes harder.
understand.analogyLimit: !important does not mean a declaration always wins in every situation. Important declarations have their own origin and layer ordering, and specificity still matters within the relevant priority group.

explain.narrative: Use !important sparingly, not as a shortcut for understanding specificity. First inspect which declaration wins, simplify selectors, remove duplicate rules, or adjust component structure. Important declarations can be appropriate for carefully scoped utility rules or when overriding third-party CSS that cannot be changed, but avoid scattering them through normal component styles. User-important declarations can outrank author-important declarations, which is important for accessibility.

examples.code: Important priority sample
examples.explanation: The .message rule sets a blue border. The .warning rule uses !important and wins despite appearing earlier. Remove !important and compare the result; both selectors have equal class specificity so source order then decides.
examples.expectedOutput: The element appears according to the winning CSS rule described in the explanation.

practise.guidedTask: Inspect the two rules, remove !important, and move the .message rule below .warning. Observe the cascade result.
practise.independentTask: Refactor a sample stylesheet containing several !important declarations into simpler selectors and a clear source order. Explain each change.
hints: Do not add !important before checking specificity and source order.
Keep focus and user preference styles accessible.

questions.prompt: Why should !important not be used routinely?
options: It can make future overrides and maintenance harder
questions.answer: It can make future overrides and maintenance harder
questions.explanation: Important declarations create a stronger priority that is harder to override.

questions.prompt: What should you inspect before adding !important?
questions.explanation: Use developer tools and understand the cascade first.
